annotator_problems: Pitch 1 has no valid decision frame under convention v2 and is reported unavailable: the broadcast holds an Albies home-run close-up through 2196.60, an SNY logo transition wipe covers the pitcher and most of the batter from 2196.75 through 2197.35, and the first clear live frames at 2197.40/2197.45 already show Megill in his delivery (release bracketed 2197.70-2197.80). This is a directly observed absence, not a fetch or viewing failure.

The bug's lower banner flickers between the pitch clock, P:N and the speed readout, and single frames catch it mid-redraw (e.g. 2197.85, 2211.40, 2211.45 show a partly drawn clock field). Every value reported was confirmed on at least two neighbouring frames.

Speed readings differ from the brief's anchor wording: I read 89 MPH on the bug from 2198.25 to 2200.50 (pitch 1) and 96 MPH from 2212.50 to 2216.00 (pitch 2). The brief described the 2215 frame's 96 MPH as following pitch 1; what I read is that 96 MPH belongs to pitch 2 and 89 MPH to pitch 1.
The batter line reads '3. OZUNA   0-1'; that trailing 0-1 is his game line, not the count. The count field in the bug reads 0-0 before pitch 1 and 0-1 before pitch 2.

Half-size montage tiles are easy to misjudge: I first mistook the pitch-1 follow-through at 2198.00 for a leg lift and read the p22_p2a frames as non-monotonic. Both were resolved by opening the raw 1280x720 frames, and only raw-frame readings are reported, but it is a reminder that montage-only posture calls are unreliable.

Sampling is 0.05 s at best and the source is a remote MP4 read frame by frame, so release times are manual estimates with uncertainty 0.15 s, not frame-exact; the pitch-2 motion start at 2210.35 is likewise the first sampled frame with movement (2210.30 was still).

annotator_problems: The half-size <label>_full.png montage is not reliable for pose reading: at that scale I first read the 2273.00 cell as a leg lift, but the raw 1280x720 frame shows Megill standing still on the rubber with the glove at his chest. At the pitch 1 and pitch 4 decision frames the bug's second banner line (the batter) was not on screen - only the MEGILL pitcher line. '4. OLSON  0-1' was read 1.25 s later at 2255.00 for pitch 1 and 0.25 s later at 2318.50 for pitch 4, both inside the same continuous live shot, so batter identity at the decision frame rests on the visible left-handed hitter plus that nearby banner rather than on the banner at t itself.
Release times are bracketed to 0.05-0.10 s but the true ball-leaves-hand instant lies inside the bracket, and the reported uncertainty of 0.15 s is a manual estimate; these are not frame-exact.

This is selected-frame review, not continuous playback. A break shorter than the sampling step (under 0.25 s at a decision boundary, under 0.50-1.00 s inside a prep window) could have been missed, particularly in the pitch 2 and pitch 3 prep windows where the gap reaches 1.00 s.

Megill's back number read as '39' at native resolution in two centre-field frames; a 4x enlargement of the 2269.50 frame resolved it as 'MEGILL 38'. I flag it because the raw-resolution reading was genuinely ambiguous.

annotator_problems: Pitch 1 decision is a judgement call on the batter, not on the shot. The live high third-base-side wide angle (pitcher on the rubber and batter both visible) already starts at 2582.50, but d'Arnaud is bent over at the waist adjusting his gear at 2583.50 and 2584.00 and only straightens up facing the pitcher at 2584.25. I treated 'bent over, looking down' as failing condition (3). A reviewer who counts a batter who is physically inside the box regardless of posture would push pitch 1's decision back to 2582.50.

Two of the five decision frames are not on the centre-field camera. Pitch 1 uses a live high third-base-side wide angle (first base is screen-right there); the feed cuts to the centre-field camera at 2590.75, i.e. after the decision and before the motion start, and I did not treat that live-to-live cut as a continuity break. Pitch 5 uses a live high upper-deck-behind-home wide angle in which the pitcher and batter are only about 30-40 px tall at 2689.75; I verified from enlarged crops that Megill is on the rubber and still and that d'Arnaud is in the box with the bat up, but the readability of the players (not the bug) is weaker than on the centre-field shots.

At pitch 4's decision frame (2669.50) the bug's lower banner is replaced by 'OFFICIAL SCORING: PASSED BALL', so the pitcher name, pitch clock, P:65 and the batter line are not printed there. The score, runners, outs, inning and count are all fully visible, so I recorded readability 'readable' with every observed field filled; P:65 was read on the same uninterrupted live shot at 2673.00 and 2674.50 and the batter banner at 2674.00.

The runners' advance from first-and-second to second-and-third between pitch 3 and pitch 4 is a passed ball as read on screen, not a steal: the SNY 'OFFICIAL SCORING: PASSED BALL' graphic is up from 2668.00 to 2672.00, the catcher is chasing the ball up the line at 2644.00, and a Braves runner is standing at third with third-base coach Tuiasosopo (89) at 2646.00. The bug's runner diamonds change from top+lower-right gold (2610-2640) to top+left gold (2668 onward), matching second and third with first base empty.

Pitch 5's motion start (2694.25) falls on the overhead wide angle and the feed cuts to the centre-field camera between 2694.50 and 2695.00, i.e. after the motion has already begun, so the last 1.2 s before release were reviewed across a camera change. This does not affect the decision frame but means the leg-lift frame and the release frame come from different cameras.

Timing precision limits: the decision search is on the 0.25 s grid and release brackets are 0.05-0.10 s wide, all from ffmpeg still grabs. Anything that happened strictly between two sampled frames (a very brief step-off, a one-frame white bug wipe) would not be visible, so continuity is asserted only at the sampled times listed in prep_sample_times.

At 2697.00 the batter is turning away from the plate and the catcher is up and moving. By 2698.00 the bug has changed to NYM 0 / ATL 2 / bases empty (all three diamonds outline) / 'END 3' in place of the inning arrow / 0-0 with both out circles cleared, over a Mets crowd shot; 2700.00 shows the same 'END 3' bug over a Braves dugout close-up. So the third out and the end of the bottom of the third are confirmed between 2696.50 and 2698.00.

annotator_problems: The task's anchor list did not mention a pickoff: Megill's motion at about 2104.75-2105.30 is a throw to first base, not pitch 4. The first-base camera at 2105.40-2105.55 shows Alonso taking the throw with Harris II diving back, and the bug still reads 1-2 P:48 at 2108. A naive reading of the anchors would have timed pitch 4 at roughly 2105.5 instead of 2124.9. The pickoff broke the otherwise valid window that had opened at 2101.50 (previous grid 2101.25 was a booth-to-field cross-dissolve).

Pitch 3's previous_grid frame (2077.00) is judgement-dependent. It is a LIVE high third-base-side aerial of the whole park, not a replay or a graphic, and the bug is readable; zoomed in, the batter, catcher and umpire are identifiable and a figure is standing on the mound, but the pitcher is only a few pixels and I could not confirm his pivot foot on the rubber or that he was still rather than starting. I therefore treated it as failing condition (1)/(2) and set the decision at 2077.25 (centre-field camera). If a reviewer accepts that aerial as a valid live wide angle, pitch 3's decision would move back to roughly 2069-2070, when the aerial began.
The bug's speed field for pitch 4 reads 97 MPH at 2128.00. That is high for Megill and I report it only as read; I did not verify it against any other source.

At pitch 1's decision frame (2040.75) the bug's second line is still the MLB.TV logo, so no batter banner is present there; '2. ALBIES BB' is first legible at 2041.00. All score/count/base/out/inning fields were readable at 2040.75, so readability is 'readable' rather than 'partial', but the batter identification for pitch 1 comes from a neighbouring frame.

Pitch 1's previous_grid failure (2040.50) is an animated SNY transition wipe painted over the live picture rather than a true cutaway; 2040.25 is the same wipe covering nearly the whole frame. I classified it as cutaway_or_replay because the convention names a transition wipe as not usable.

The small pitch-clock digits on the bug are the least reliable field at this resolution; neighbouring 0.25 s frames occasionally read ambiguously between :06 and :07. The count, P:N, base diamonds, out circles, inning arrow and scores were unambiguous at every decision frame.

All times are manual estimates from selected ffmpeg frame grabs at 0.05 s spacing around release and 0.25 s spacing on the decision grid, not continuous playback; uncertainty_seconds is 0.15 for every row and none of these should be treated as frame-exact. Motion-start values are the first SAMPLED frame showing the leg lift, so the true onset can be up to one sampling step earlier.

annotator_problems: Pitch 4 decision frame is the least clean of the five: at 2459.75 Megill is at the rubber but appears to be settling his feet onto it rather than fully still (at 2460.00 he is unambiguously standing on it). A stricter reading of condition 2 would move decision_seconds to 2460.00. Reported 2459.75 because he is already on the rubber, facing the plate, with no rocker step or leg lift.

The bug alternates the pitch clock and the P:N field, so at the pitch 3 and pitch 4 decision frames (2440.75, 2459.75) no pitch clock was displayed; P:58 and P:59 were read directly from those same frames, not from neighbours.

The batter banner was not visible at two decision frames: absent at 2396.25 (it appears at 2397.50 as '5. SOLER  0-1') and covered by the MLB.TV logo at 2487.50 (read as 's. SOLER  0-1' at 2476.00). Reported as batter_banner_seen text rather than claimed as read at the decision second.

Pitch 5 has a very short pre-pitch window: the broadcast is on an on-deck/dugout cutaway from 2478 through 2487.25 and returns only 0.75 s before the leg lift, so prep_sample_times has only three frames (2487.50, 2488.00, 2488.25).

The 0.25 s grid search means the true cut back to the live shot can be up to 0.25 s earlier than each reported decision second; I verified the preceding grid point is a cutaway in all five cases but did not sample below 0.25 s resolution.
Release times are manual brackets: the pre-release and post-release frames are 0.05-0.10 s apart, so 0.15 s uncertainty is claimed and no frame-exact release is asserted.

The SNY bug lags play by 2-3 s, so outcome-driven changes trail the pitch (e.g. 95 MPH / 0-1 first appears at 2404 for the pitch released at 2400.60, 88 MPH at 2490.00 for the pitch released at 2489.10). Decision-frame readings are unaffected because the count had settled well before each delivery.
Megill's uniform number reads as '33' or '39' in some motion-blurred frames (2463, 2464) but is clearly 38 in sharp frames; this is motion blur, not a different pitcher.

Observed values matched the stated expectation at every decision frame (NYM 0 / ATL 2, 1 out, runner on 1B only, bottom 3, counts 0-0/0-1/0-2/1-2/2-2 with P:56-P:60). Nothing was copied from the expectation - each was read off the enlarged bug crop - but nothing contradicted it either, so there is no discrepancy to flag.

Supporting frames: at 2490.00/2490.50 the bug still shows 2-2 with '88 MPH' while the ball is in the air (bug lag), and the next live pre-pitch state after the PA is the 0-0 / two-out / P:61 bug at 2505.00.

annotator_problems: Pitch 6 has no valid v2 decision frame and is reported unavailable. The broadcast held extreme close-ups of Megill alone (no batter, no rubber) from about 1982.0 through 1984.75 and cut back to the centre-field shot at exactly 1985.00, by which point the leg lift had already begun. I verified this directly on the raw 1985.00 frame. Its release was nevertheless observed (bracket 1985.75 / 1985.90) and is recorded in the note only, with the row's times left null per the convention.

At the pitch-1 decision frame (1894.25) the lower banner shows only 'MEGILL :09 P:38'; the '1. HARRIS II 0-1' batter line is not yet displayed. It first appears at 1896.50 and is present at every later decision frame in the PA, so the batter identity at 1894.25 rests on the live image plus the banner 2.25 s later rather than on a banner in that frame.

Pitches 5 and 6 both read 2-2 on the bug; they are distinguished only by the pitch-count banner (P:42 vs P:43) and by order in time. The banner lags plays by 2-3 s, so this separation, while directly read, inherits that lag.

Outcomes were not verified independently of the bug. What I read is the count progression 0-0 -> 1-0 (after pitch 1), 1-0 -> 1-1 (after pitch 2), 1-1 -> 1-2 (after pitch 3), 1-2 -> 2-2 (after pitch 4), 2-2 held after pitches 5 and 6, and a runner on first with the count reset after pitch 7. This is consistent with the expected ball / swinging_strike / foul / ball / foul / foul / single sequence but does not by itself confirm swinging_strike vs called strike, or foul vs foul tip.

The bug is fully white during a transition wipe at 1893.50 (unreadable). That frame lies before the pitch-1 decision frame and outside every continuity window, so it affects nothing, but it is the only wipe I saw in this PA.

Release times rest on 0.05-0.10 s brackets from a remote MP4 read by ffmpeg seek; sub-frame alignment was not attempted and uncertainty_seconds is 0.15 for every annotated pitch. Decision frames are on the 0.25 s grid, so the true shot-change and motion-start instants lie within 0.25 s below the reported values.

No repository file was created, edited or committed; only frame images were written under outputs/frames (labels p20_scanA/B/C/D/E/F/G, p20_1back, p20_1rel, p20_2back, p20_2rel, p20_3ab, p20_4back, p20_4ab, p20_5back, p20_5rel, p20_6a, p20_7a, p20_7b).
